summary: Windows Hello registration blocked by UVC camera driver present after depot repair
description:
Issue summary:

Several recently repaired Windows laptops fail Windows Hello biometric enrollment for face/IR camera at the OOBE / post-imaging first-run. The symptom: user is shown the camera preview but the enrollment flow immediately errors with a generic 'Device not ready' message. Affected devices were returned from depot repair where a third-party replacement UVC module (camera) was installed.

Impact:
- Blocks user onboarding for ~5% of depot returns that received third-party camera replacements.
- Creates repeated helpdesk escalations and physical rework (re-send to depot) currently required to get the device to a state where biometric enrollment works.

Environment:
- Windows 11 22H2 with corporate image (SCCM/OOBE flow).
- Devices repro'd in prod-us-west and lab imaging bench.
- Hardware: Dell XPS 15 9520, Lenovo X1 Carbon Gen11 with replacement UVC camera modules (non-OEM).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Re-image device with corp image and run through OOBE (Azure AD join, SCCM provisioning, Windows Hello setup).
2) At the Windows Hello / camera preview step, observe preview appears but enrollment fails quickly with error 'Device not ready'.
3) Check Device Manager / Windows logs; camera appears as 'USB Video Device (UVC)' and the driver stack lists a generic uvcvideo.sys with Timestamps matching third-party firmware.

Observed behavior:
- Windows Hello enrollment fails immediately; Windows logs show Windows Biometric Framework (WBF) reports Error 0xC0000225 / STATUS_NOT_FOUND for WBF sensor interface. Device Manager shows 'This device cannot start (Code 10)' intermittently for camera device.

Expected behavior:
- Camera preview and enrollment complete normally under OOBE; WBF binds to the proper sensor component.

Initial triage notes:
- Support (Maya) validated multiple repros on our imaging bench using new replacement cameras from Depot vendor 'CamPro Solutions'.
- Local testing: replacing the third-party camera with OEM camera resolves the issue consistently.
- Kernel-mode driver (uvcvideo) appears to load, but WBF fails to enumerate a compatible sensor interface (Sensor Class GUID mismatch in driver descriptors).

Logs / snippets:
- Event Viewer (System) around time of failure:
  - Source: Service Control Manager - EventID 7009 - 'A timeout was reached... Windows Biometric Service failed to start'
  - Source: WBF - EventID 501 - 'No compatible sensor found (GUID mismatch)'
- Device Manager registry keys: 
  HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Enum\USB\VID_0C45&PID_6366 --- DeviceDesc = "USB Video Device"
  Driver stack: uvcvideo.sys -> usbvideo.sys -> usbd.sys

Workaround attempted:
- Manually installing vendor-supplied camera driver package from CamPro (signed) allowed the camera to present a different descriptor but still did not expose the WBF sensor.
- Replacing camera with OEM hardware resolves issue.
- Short-term mitigation: helpdesk script added to check Device Manager and escalate to Hardware if the camera device reports Code 10. Script link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/IT/Depot+Repair+Post-Image+Checks

Investigation hypothesis:
- Third-party camera firmware/descriptor does not expose the sensor interface type WBF expects (missing or incorrect camera sensor GUID or metadata). WBF refuses to register the sensor despite UVC consumer preview working.
- Alternative root cause: image-level security policies (driver block list) could be interfering with non-OEM driver bindings under the new security baseline, but lab installs with driver signing bypass did not fix enrollment.

Next steps:
- Jamal to capture a full USB descriptor dump from affected camera and compare against OEM camera descriptors (task created).
- Hardware/Depot team to block non-OEM camera SKUs pending firmware fix from CamPro.
- Eng/Platform to add an automation check in depot return pipeline to detect cameras that do not expose WBF sensor descriptors (low-effort USB descriptor check).

Attachments:
- usb-descriptor-dump-INT505050-0310.txt (attached to issue in Jira UI)
steps_to_reproduce: Re-image device with corp image and run OOBE/Windows Hello
Observe camera preview then immediate 'Device not ready' error
Check Device Manager for 'USB Video Device' and Code 10

resolution: In Progress - short-term mitigations implemented (depot quarantine + imaging bench descriptor check + helpdesk script). Root cause tracked to third-party camera firmware descriptor not exposing required WBF sensor interface. Awaiting vendor firmware update; Engineering to test firmware when provided.
resolution_notes: If vendor supplies firmware patch that updates USB descriptors to include WBF-compatible sensor properties, plan: 1) obtain signed driver/firmware, 2) test on bench across affected models, 3) update Depot QA pipeline to accept patched units, 4) release guidance to field. If vendor cannot remediate, Depot will revert to OEM replacements and vendor will be delisted.
